question.text: How long must KYC records of investors be retained under PMLA (Maintenance of Records) Rules as discussed in the AIF workbook?

answer.text: 2 years from the date of transaction
3 years from the date of KYC update
Minimum 5 years from the date of cessation of transactions (with litigation retention until completion of proceedings)
10 years from the date of fund wind-up

explanation.text: The Logic: KYC records should be maintained for a minimum of 5 years from cessation of transactions with the client, with litigation retention until completion of proceedings. The retention clock runs from cessation, not the date of the underlying transaction. The Trap: Options A and B understate retention. Option D (10 years from wind-up) is a different statutory regime, not PMLA KYC retention. Note: Workbook page 383 supports the 5-year KYC retention from cessation and the litigation-pending retention rule; page 382 supports related transaction-record and client due-diligence obligations.
